title: Ethanol Quantification Assay
author: Marcos Valenzuela-Ortega
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bnuemete

steps.title: Prepare enzyme and cofactor stocks
steps.instruction: Dissolve each reagent in tris buffer to the following concentrations: Yeast ADH 5 mg/mL (20 mM, Mw 685.41), NAD⁺ 13.3 mg/mL (20 mM, Mw 685.41), PMS 6.1 mg/mL (20 mM, Mw 306.34), INTV 25.3 mg/mL (50 mM, Mw 505.00). Dissolve INTV in a 1:1 buffer‑DMSO mixture. Keep all reagent stocks on ice; keep the tris buffer at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare ethanol standard ladder
steps.instruction: Make an ethanol standard ladder by diluting 1 M ethanol stock with tris buffer to obtain final concentrations of 400, 200, 100, 50, 25, 10, 5, and 0 mM ethanol.

steps.title: Process culture samples
steps.instruction: Aliquot culture, centrifuge at 16,000 rpm for 1 min (temperature °C as indicated). Transfer supernatant to a new tube. Keep on ice if the assay will be performed immediately; otherwise freeze for later analysis.

steps.title: Prepare reaction master mix
steps.instruction: Calculate total reaction volume as 200 µL × (number of wells) × 1.1. In that volume add per mL of final mix: Yeast ADH 5 µL, NAD⁺ 1 µL, PMS 1 µL, INTV 20 µL. Fill the remaining volume with tris buffer. Prepare the master mix for all samples and standards in a single tube.

substeps.instruction: Add Yeast ADH, NAD⁺, PMS, and INTV at the specified µL per mL ratios.
Adjust to final volume with tris buffer.

steps.title: Plan plate layout and annotate
steps.instruction: Design the plate layout, assign wells for blanks, standards, and samples, and record the map. Note that reaction mix will be added to replicates at slightly different times to capture loading variability.

steps.title: Load blanks with buffer
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of tris buffer to each blank well (these wells will not receive reaction mix).

steps.title: Add reaction mix to assay wells
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, dispense 200 µL of the prepared reaction mix into each assay well (excluding blanks) as quickly and uniformly as possible.

steps.title: Add sample to wells
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of each sample or standard to the bottom of the corresponding well, ensuring the entire volume enters the well and not the tip.

steps.title: Mix plate and incubate
steps.instruction: Mix the plate (plate reader can perform mixing) and incubate at room temperature for 15 min in the dark.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 500 nm
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 500 nm on a plate reader set to room temperature; avoid temperature fluctuations that could cause condensation.
